study_identification_part.si4_title: Developmental trajectories of neuroanatomical alterations associated with the 16p11.2 Copy Number Variations

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Characterize age-related effects of 16p11.2 CNVs on brain anatomy across a broad pediatric-to-young-adult age range using a normative developmental dataset for age/sex adjustment, and test whether alterations change with age.

rci1_dataset_name.reason: NIHPD is used as the normative reference dataset; the 16p11.2 cohort comprises European (EU) and Simons VIP (SVIP) sites.
rci1_dataset_name.supporting_text: As normative reference data for brain growth, we used the ... NIHPD project... Cross-sectional data was acquired in 2 different cohorts (the European -EU ... and the Simons VIP -SVIP).

rci2_hc_n.reason: NIHPD normative model built on 339 children with 874 scans; the study sample includes 105 control individuals for comparison and normalization checks.
rci2_hc_n.supporting_text: The normative model ... used data from 339 children ... for a total of 874 scans. ... This included ... 105 controls (CTRL).

rci3_hc_age.supporting_text: ... mean age at first scan of 11.0 years, ... Objective 1 (i.e. initial time-point for enrolment from 4.5 to 18.5 years) ... Table 1 ... CTRL Mean (SD) 14.15 (4.24); range 4.67-22.92.

rci5_imaging_modality.supporting_text: The MRI data from the 16p11.2 individuals included T1-weighted (T1w) anatomical images ...

rci6_analysis_level.supporting_text: We normalized volumes of segmented brain regions as well as volumes of each voxel defined by tensor-based morphometry.

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.answer: Denoising; N3 bias correction; histogram matching to ICBM152; linear registration to ICBM152; BEaST brain extraction; ANIMAL nonlinear registration; TBM with 10 mm FWHM smoothing; neuromorphometric atlas labeling

(3) intensity normalization by histogram matching to the ICBM152 template ... linear registration ... BEaST ... ANIMAL ... TBM ... 3D Gaussian filter FWHM 10 mm ... anatomically labeled using the neuromorphometric atlas.

rci8_quality_checking.detail: NIHPD: only QC-passed subjects included. 16p11.2: thorough visual QC for motion artifacts; no counts reported.
rci8_quality_checking.supporting_text: Only subjects that passed quality control were included. ... We performed a thorough visual quality control check looking for evidence of motion artefacts.

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: Scanner fixed effect tested in NIHPD mixed-effects modeling and excluded due to non-significance (BIC). 16p11.2 analyses included protocol (single vs multi echo) as covariate; previous study confirmed multisite effects did not drive findings.
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: ... fixed effect for individual scanner was tested but found to be not significant ... Raw values ... corrected for ... protocol ... none of the regions ... attributed to artefacts introduced by the multisite analyses (Martin-Brevet et al., 2018).

nm1_model_origin.detail: NIHPD mixed-effects normative trajectories (Aubert-Broche et al.) trained on 339 children (179F/160M) with 2–3 scans each (874 scans), modeling quadratic age and sex; used to derive mean and SD for Z-scoring of global and voxel-wise measures.
nm1_model_origin.supporting_text: The normative model ... used data from 339 children ... 874 scans ... individual profiles suggest modeling brain growth as a quadratic function ... Linear effect of sex ... mixed-effects model that best fits the normative data is: ...

nm2_modeling_method.answer: Linear mixed-effects normative model (quadratic age, sex) with Z-scoring; voxel-wise TBM using log-Jacobian determinants; group effects via linear models with interactions tested (age*sex, age*group).
nm2_modeling_method.reason: Model specification and analysis steps are explicitly described.
nm2_modeling_method.supporting_text: The mixed-effects model that best fits the normative data is: ... Z-scores ... For analyses ... We used a linear model introducing genetic status as a covariate ... interaction terms were tested: age*sex and age*group.

nm3_software_tool.reason: They state analyses were conducted in R with nlme for mixed-effects models.
nm3_software_tool.supporting_text: All analyses were conducted using R 3.4.0 ... The mixed-effect models were built using the nlme package.

nm4_response_variable.answer: Global volumes (total brain, gray matter, white matter, lateral ventricles); subcortical/ROI volumes (lobes, thalamus, putamen, caudate, globus pallidus); voxel-wise log-Jacobian determinants (TBM)
nm4_response_variable.reason: Response variables for both ROI/global and voxel-wise analyses are specified.
nm4_response_variable.supporting_text: Whole-brain, individual lobes, thalamus, putamen, caudate, globus pallidus and ventricular volumes were calculated ... TBM ... Jacobian determinant ... used as a surrogate of the local volume difference ...

nm5_predictor_variables.reason: Normative modeling included linear and quadratic age terms and sex as fixed effects.
nm5_predictor_variables.supporting_text: ... modeling brain growth as a quadratic function ... Linear effect of sex was also included in the fixed terms ...

nm6_predictor_effects.answer: Fixed effects: age (linear, quadratic), sex; Random effects: subject-level intercept and slope for age
nm6_predictor_effects.reason: The mixed-effects model equation specifies random intercept and random slope and fixed terms for age and sex.
nm6_predictor_effects.supporting_text: Vol_i = β0 + γ0 + (β1 + γ1)(Age_i-13) + β2(Age_i-13)^2 + β3 Sex_i + ε_i ... β are fixed effects; γ are random effects.

nm7_nm_vldtn_handle_ns.supporting_text: ... quadratic effects of age ... Linear effect of sex ... During model selection, a fixed effect for individual scanner was tested but found to be not significant ... we show ... model ... is robust and applies to data acquired on a 3T after a linear adjustment ... normalization ... neither sex nor age terms are significantly different than 0.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Linear models tested genetic status effects on normalized Z-scores with interactions (age*sex, age*group). Global volumes: Bonferroni correction for 8 comparisons; Voxel-wise TBM: FDR (q<0.05). No age interactions observed; stable differences across 4.5–23 years.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Inverse gene dosage effects in global and regional brain measures for 16p11.2 CNV carriers are present by ~4.5 years and remain stable through early adulthood.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Deletion carriers showed higher Z-scores vs controls for total brain (mean Z=1.165, p<0.0001), gray (Z=0.414, p=0.00433) and white matter (Z=0.693, p<0.0001), whereas duplication carriers showed lower Z-scores (total brain Z=-1.17, p=0.0001; gray Z=-0.631, p=0.00272; white Z=-0.53, p=0.0018) and larger lateral ventricles (Z=1.629, p<0.0001). TBM revealed DEL>CTRL>DUP in bilateral calcarine cortex and insula, among others. No age*group interactions; effects stable across 4.5–23 years.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Normalization approach enables cross-age analysis using external normative trajectories; authors suggest future refinements with 3T longitudinal data and alternative modeling (e.g., splines) to better capture variability.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Acquisition differences between normative (1.5T) and study (3T) data and multicenter variability may affect registrations; limited power for detecting small age-related changes (especially in DUP) and uncertainty at lower age range; generalizability may be limited for extreme obesity or severe ASD unable to complete scanning.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: NIHPD ancestry composition similar to 16p11.2 cohort; analyses conducted in R 3.4.0 (nlme); labeling via neuromorphometric atlas; prior multisite artifact checks cited (Martin-Brevet 2018).
